doc.citation: García Muro, V. J., Rubinstein, C. V. & Steemans, P. 2014. Upper Silurian miospores from the Precordillera Basin, Argentina: biostratigraphic, palaeoenvironmental and palaeogeographic implications. Geological Magazine 151(3), 472–490.
doc.comment: Fourteen productive samples and four barren samples were studied. Authors favour Ludlow, allowing Pridoli for the youngest samples despite some apparently Devonian taxa. Hispanaediscus wenlockensis could be reworked. Figure 4 was inspected in the local PDF: dotted supposed ranges are excluded; dashed occurrences receive cf. qualifiers. Plate-caption occurrences are retained where they supplement or conflict with Figure 4, including Retusotriletes sp. and Emphanisporites protophanus in sample 13. Illustration flags are sample-specific. Qualifier differences between plates and the range chart are preserved. The paper reports new Quebrada Ancha material; comparisons with earlier publications are not treated as new assemblages. A [published corrigendum](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/geological-magazine/article/upper-silurian-miospores-from-the-precordillera-basin-argentina-biostratigraphic-palaeoenvironmental-and-palaeogeographic-implications-corrigendum/E363F15CF1565CC4DD1C7DF296CDB70A) replaces Figure 2; its corrected figure was not available for inspection. Numerical sample levels below follow Figure 4.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha area, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Sample 1 (60667); 0,2 m from the base of the formation
items.age_basis_detail: Miospore biozone correlations and marine phytoplankton. Chelinospora verrucata indicates an age no older than the base of the LP Biozone, interpreted as latest Homerian or earliest Gorstian; acritarchs support Ludlow.
items.notes: Lowest productive sample. Overall palynological assemblages contain abundant marine acritarchs and chlorophytes.

items.notes: Section 6 explicitly reports Concentricosisporites agradabilis here, although Figure 4 starts its observed range in sample 3. Archaeozonotriletes chulus is dashed in Figure 4 and therefore qualified cf.

items.age_basis_detail: Miospores and marine phytoplankton. Amicosporites streelii suggests Lochkovian, but similar specimens are reported from the Upper Silurian of Saudi Arabia. Authors retain Ludlow with possible Pridoli for youngest samples.
items.setting_as_reported: storm-dominated shelf and shoreface environments; subaerial exposures at the top of the regression cycles
items.notes: Figure 8b records Emphanisporites protophanus here, beyond its Figure 4 observed range. Figure 7o adds Retusotriletes sp., absent from the systematic list and Figure 4. Figure 6l gives slide 600984 for cf. Concentricosisporites sagittarius; Figure 4 places this taxon in sample 13 (60984), indicating an apparent caption typo. Chelinospora obscura is dashed in Figure 4. Amicosporites streelii is treated partim because specimens grouped under that name may represent different species.

items.locality: Quebrada Ancha area, near Talacasto, Central Precordillera, San Juan Province
items.depth_or_level: Samples 15 (60980), 16 (60978), 17 (60977) and 18 (60976); the four samples closest to the upper boundary
items.age_basis_detail: Age assigned to the studied succession from productive samples and previously reported fauna; these four samples provide no palynological age evidence.
items.setting_as_reported: storm-dominated shelf and shoreface environments; subaerial exposures at the top of the regression cycles
items.notes: Spores were sought but not found: all four samples were barren. The paper describes complete disappearance of palynomorphs near the top, potentially associated with storm-dominated platform to shoreface facies and subaerial exposure. Their age is inherited partly from spore correlations elsewhere in the studied succession, rather than independently established in these barren samples.
